keyFindings.description: The invariant holds in the code, but no test locks the two parts of callKeys that close the review of 0c1e3cf4's findings. With the upload key dropped (uploads keyed by their asks, or the whole call when none), the whole askgate.test.ts passes (382 pass, 0 fail), while a no-ask notes.md refused twice lets a different no-ask other.md out on the breaker (that review's second finding), a same-named upload with other prose passes on the old text's refusals, and a fully stored brief.md's refusals count its stored #window so a later brief.md adding #gamma passes unreviewed. With the content digest dropped from the upload key the suite also passes and the same-named-other-text case passes on the breaker. The new test 'after two charter refusals of one upload on an issue, a different upload there with no ask block is reviewed' refuses brief.md, which carries an ask block, so it does not exercise the no-ask case it names. Verified by the reviewer in a scratch copy and by the quality review's mutants M2 and M4. Fix: three tests that fail under those mutants — two no-ask uploads of different documents (the second reviewed), a same-named upload with changed text (reviewed), and a fully stored re-upload refused twice followed by the same name adding a new ask (reviewed).

invariant: Holds in the code. callKeys (askgate-core.ts:2529) is the one key set; breaker.tripped (:3352) reads it; refusalThings (:2558) counts only keys of the refused call and never none, so a warned resend trips and no loop on one call is endless. Upload keys are JSON arrays with a fixed tag and a sha256 of the text, so agent text cannot forge another upload's key (deep review's forgery probes).
probes: The reviewer's adversarial pass, results per send 1/2/3: rules unjudged and rules error refuse/refuse+warn/breaker; warn-mode charter revise no count and no warning; warn-mode rules match refuse/refuse+warn/breaker; same name with other text and another no-ask document reviewed; comment and doc-edit refuse/refuse+warn/breaker; unreadable never counted or warned. The three new tests fail with askgate-core.ts from 0c1e3cf4. The deep review (APPROVE) probed key forgery: whitespace in the name trips as Dispatch trims it, a case change does not, --path then --content-file with the same text trips, an ask spelling an upload key does not.
judgedNotDefects: A call trips on any one of its keys, so asks beside a twice-refused ask go out with it (the approved per-thing design), and the partly judged upload's third send (the architect's ruling).

The quality review's cross-document case: an ask block refused twice in one upload trips another document's upload on the same issue carrying the same block. The breaker target for an upload is the issue (#2159's BREAKER_KEYS), and the passing thing is the same ask refused twice, the spec's 'a third copy of the same refused ask also opens'; what rides beside it is the per-thing design above. Reported to the architect.
